targets.title: Training supervisors to provide performance feedback using video modeling with voiceover instructions.
targets.evidence_quote:
In the current study, we sought to replicate the
research by Shuler and Carroll (2019) in a new
setting with additional participants.
targets.outcome_quote:
Overall, the results of Study 1 replicate the
ﬁndings of Shuler and Carroll (2019). All ﬁve
supervisors acquired the steps of the performance feedback procedure after watching the
video model.

targets.authors: Parsons, M. B., & Reid, D. H.
targets.title: Training residential supervisors to provide feedback for maintaining staff teaching skills with people who have severe disabilities.
targets.evidence_quote:
The results of Study 2 extend ﬁndings of
previous studies (Parsons & Reid, 1995;
Shuler & Carroll, 2019), by demonstrating that
therapists’
guided-compliance
integrity
increased after receiving performance feedback
from one of the supervisors trained in Study
1. All three therapists in Study 2 reached our
mastery criterion following three to six feedback sessions (M = four sessions).

reasoning: Verified title, DOI, authors, and full article pages 603–621. Study 1 directly repeats Shuler and Carroll with new supervisors. Study 2 retests the therapist-performance finding of Parsons and Reid: the authors explicitly connect improvement after supervisor feedback to that earlier work; Shuler did not measure therapist improvement, so Parsons is the closest relevant target for that claim. Child compliance is incidental, not the central retested finding.
